definition: In this packet, conditional reasoning refers to an assessment approach that uses how people reason through items to detect less obvious, implicit tendencies rather than relying only on direct self-report. Here it is used to assess implicit aggression through reasoning patterns linked to biases such as hostile attribution, revenge, and social discounting.

reasons: The packet does not explicitly define “conditional reasoning” as a general assessment approach (e.g., “how people reason through items”)—it describes the development/validation of an “implicit aggression conditional reasoning test” but does not clearly provide the requested term definition in those words.

The “conditional reasoning” rationale (detecting implicit tendencies rather than relying only on direct self-report) is only indirectly supported by general statements contrasting self-report with implicit aggression; the packet does not directly link that contrast to the meaning of “conditional reasoning” itself.

While the packet supports that the test includes dimensions/biases including hostility attribution bias, revenge bias, and social discounting bias, it does not substantiate the broader definitional framing that these are “reasoning patterns linked to biases” as the defining sense of the term.
